why: Same notions (IsGoodLeftProj = Π_T, Submodule.IsTopCompl, operator norm); A's (e : Y →L R(P)) = projRestrict P S Y is B's pointwise e y = P (S y). A has no hypothesis that T is Fredholm, B has one, so A => B is instantiation. B => A is not instantiation: B is applied to a different Fredholm operator, T'' = P T|_Y : Y → F on the closed (Banach) subspace Y, which is injective with range R(PT) = R(P) (closed, finite codimension), hence Fredholm (project lemma isFredholm_of_banach), with P ∈ Π_{T''}, ker(PT'') = 0 and complement ⊤. For ‖S − T‖ < ε'/(‖P‖+1), S'' = P S|_Y is within ε' of T'', so B gives R(PS'') = R(P) (hence R(PS) = R(P)) and an isomorphism ⊤ ≅ R(P), y ↦ P S y, whence P S|_Y is bijective and, by the open mapping theorem, a topological isomorphism. So the Fredholm hypothesis on T is inessential and the two statements are equivalent.
